messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — Hosted API region us-west-2 p99 latency > 15s for 5m, queue depth 12,400, 502/504s rising. Autoscaler events show repeated pool-create failures. Paging oncall: @alex (oncall) :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): seeing it, joining. thx bot. is this across all models or a particular family?

maya (sre): most traffic hitting gpt-lite-variants and some customer pinned to gpt-8-large. Metrics: GPU pool saturation + create API 429 from cloud provider starting ~09:04 UTC. Provisioner logs show "quota_exceeded" and some rate-limit backoff loops.

devon (runtime): autoscaler tried to spin 18 new GPU nodes, cloud returned 429/403 for ~70% of calls. when it did succeed, pods hit OOM on init due to image pull delay and kernel mismatch. stack:
```
Provisioner -> cloud-API POST /instances -> 429 (quota)
k8s -> pod Pending -> ImagePullBackOff
runtime -> model load timed out (kv init)
```

tara (support): we're getting multiple customer reports — some timeouts in prod, large customers seeing retries and elevated client-side latencies. ticket queue spike. @sam can you check top affected orgs?

sam (customer-success): pulling list now. Top affected: AcmeSight (high traffic), BeaconPay (critical), 3 smaller beta customers. I've DM'd account owners and opened on-call bridge for customer alerts.

alex (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller quantized variants for non-pinned requests, 2) throttle new non-paid free-tier requests, 3) preemptively re-route traffic to eu-west or dedicated pools for key customers. can devon/maya triage feasibility?

devon (runtime): we can flip a routing policy quickly for hosted-paid vs free tiers. small patch to router config, 2–3 minute rollout. quantized fallbacks require model-compat checks but we have gpt-lite-q available in us-west in limited pools.

maya (sre): autoscaler health: leader election flapping in provisioner due to ephemeral DB latency; when provisioner fails leader elect, autoscaler loop pauses and retries -> backlog growth. ops-bot shows 47 provisioner retries in last 10m.

ops-bot: provisioner-retries: 47; cloud-429-count: 1532; gpu-pools-active: 84/84 (hard cap); image-pull-failures: 12 in last 7m.

alex (oncall): plan: 1) throttle anonymous/free traffic by 50% immediate (maya + devon) 2) enable fallback routing for paid customers to gpt-lite-q where possible (devon) 3) open expedited quota request with cloud and escalate with partner rep (maya) 4) short-term targeted rate-limits per org (tara + sam) 5) monitor tail latencies and backlog. I'll take incident commander until handoff.

tara (support): applying rate-limits now to free keys. pushing a soft 429 for anonymous keys. will post exact rule in a sec.

(devon pasted): Router change snippet:
```
# roll: enable-lite-fallback=true
route.rules.hosted: if (customer.tier != 'free' && model.compat('gpt-lite-q')) -> model=gpt-lite-q
push config -> router-prod (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
```

maya (sre): canary to 10% started at 09:18 UTC. initial success: backlog drop from 12.4k -> 9.1k in 3m. p95 down ~1.8s for routed traffic. but still overall p99 elevated.

sam (customer-success): AcmeSight reports some degraded responses but accepts fallback for now. BeaconPay is on a pinned dedicated contract — not eligible for fallback; their route still stuck in queue and seeing 504s.

alex (oncall): for pinned critical customers we need direct action: check dedicated pool availability, maybe burst them to a reserved dedicated cluster in eu-west if legal. devon/maya evaluate cross-region failover risk (latency + data residency).

devon (runtime): quick check: we have two dedicated reserved pools in eu-west with spare headroom (approx 25%). Migration for an org requires key-level routing change; can be done via console API. ETA ~8–12 minutes per org for config + verification.

maya (sre): opening quota escalation w/ cloud support now. Uploading logs and "impacting production" flag. also starting a temporary leader restart of provisioner to clear elect flapping. I'll coordinate with infra.

ops-bot: cloud-support-ticket: 12345 created (priority=P1).

alex (oncall): execute: tara/sam — apply per-org emergency rate-limits for BeaconPay? we want to reduce retries and tail latency while we migrate. tara, can you contact BeaconPay ops?

tara (support): pinging BeaconPay ops now via slack and email. proposing a short failover window to eu-west; asking for approval.

(devon): small ops trick: we can temporarily enable a degraded-mode that allows returning 503 with a helpful Retry-After for non-critical customers to reduce retry storms. toggled as last resort.

maya (sre): leader restart initiated for provisioner at 09:26 UTC. watching cluster.

ops-bot: provisioner-restart: success (09:27 UTC). leader election stable. retries dropping.

alex (oncall): status check: backlog 9.1k -> 5.6k after canary ramp and free-tier throttle. p95 improved, p99 still ~8–12s for some heavy requests. cloud 429s decreased by 70% since escalation.

sam (customer-success): BeaconPay approved cross-region migration for emergency window. starting routing change now.

devon (runtime): applied routing change for BeaconPay to dedicated eu-west pool at 09:34 UTC. verification: BeaconPay requests now showing <500ms in eu-west, no errors.

tara (support): notified BeaconPay success, monitoring for errors.

maya (sre): autoscaler loop healthy, provisioner stable. still seeing occasional image-pull latency spikes; ops team investigating registry peering.

alex (oncall): ok we have triage -> mitigation loop moving. next actions: 1) continue cloud quota escalation and await permanent increases 2) run post-incident regression on autoscaler leader election fixes (maya/devon) 3) refine router fallback to exclude latency-sensitive pinned orgs automatically 4) customer comms draft (sam/tara). I'll keep incident commander until handed to morning SRE shift at 11:00 UTC.

sam (customer-success): drafting customer comms: short summary + mitigation + ETA for follow-up postmortem. will share in #incidents-digest.

devon (runtime): putting a short-term automation: if provisioner-retries > 30 in 10m, emit runbook step to restart leader and notify infra.

maya (sre): will open GitHub issue for root-cause on leader flapping + image-pull delays and assign to eng-infra and runtime. severity: Sev2.

alex (oncall): final status at 09:59 UTC: backlog 1.2k, p95 in target, p99 ~3s for some large payloads, key customers routed or mitigated. keeping pager open for another 60m for monitoring. preparing handoff notes to morning shift.

ops-bot: incident-note-saved -> link: https://redwood-internal/incident/INC-1960012345

tara (support): closing customer tickets that had been resolved, leaving follow-up open for AcmeSight to verify 24h.

sam (customer-success): sending comms to affected customers.

alex (oncall): handing incident to @maya for postmortem tracking and follow-up. thanks all — good coordination. :heroic:

maya (sre): acknowledged handoff. will own postmortem and action items. created tracker: https://redwood-internal/pm/INC-1960012345-actions

ops-bot: incident-closed (status=mitigated) at 10:12 UTC.

(End of thread)
